source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #293 (branch fix/191-jit-direct-calls at head 1fa6db7889158ac6d1eb8abc1c9d573bf19378d7 — branch commit f0015b9 (enter JIT callees directly on native-to-native calls (#191)), merge commit 159796d bringing in main 41bca95 (PR #290, #190), commit de0de8f bounding native entry by the host stack (Codex P1 fix), and merge commit 1fa6db7 bringing in current main 1b25df0 (PR #291, #137); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45327945752 and 45327956071 against the branch and pull-request run 45327889910, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Second re-baseline for PR #293 (#191, JIT-to-JIT calls round-tripping through the runtime with a per-call mutex), after the Codex P1 fix de0de8f and the merge of current main (1b25df0, PR #291). The P1 fix bounds native entry by the host stack: both native entry boundaries (generic enter_current_frame_raw and direct enter_compiled_from_jit_call) compare the current stack pointer against a floor recorded on the ExecuteContext (the executing thread's OS stack low bound plus a 256 KiB reserve, established lazily at first entry, with a fixed 512 KiB budget as fallback), and decline the entry through the existing fallback results when the remaining stack runs low, so deep guest recursion reaches the value-stack StackOverflow instead of aborting the process on small host stacks. No TLS and no depth counter are reintroduced. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone (workflow_dispatch run 45327968623, gate success): it reproduces the pre-#191 baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta below is this PR's own. Against main, 18 of the 32 gated series change. In release, core-jit grows by 1,904 B stripped file / 1,616 B stripped .text, core-aot grows by 32 B stripped .text only, and component, core, core-nosimd, wasi and wasi-threads each grow by 16 B / 16 B (the ExecuteContext stack-floor field in shared code). In release-size, core-jit grows by 896 B / 688 B, core-aot shrinks by 128 B / 80 B, and wasi grows by 16 B stripped .text only. Against the first PR #293 re-baseline (head efe8dea), the increment attributable to the P1 fix alone is: release core-jit +752 B / +640 B, core-aot +560 B / +480 B, and +16 B / +16 B on component, core, core-nosimd, wasi and wasi-threads; release-size core-jit +624 B / +448 B, core-aot +320 B / +224 B, wasi +16 B stripped .text. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series, unchanged at +9.59% (2,433,656 B to 2,667,136 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
